name: Asset Plus Limited
sector: NZ Commercial Property (REIT-like, externally managed, single-asset wind-down)
overview: Asset Plus Limited (formerly NPT Limited) is an NZX-listed commercial property investment company, externally managed by Centuria Funds Management (NZ) Limited. Following the November 2024 sale of 35 Graham Street, the company now owns a single asset, the 6-8 Munroe Lane office building in Albany, Auckland, valued at $105.5 million as at 31 March 2026. Management's stated strategy is to complete the lease-up of Munroe Lane, then sell the property and put an orderly wind-up of the Company to a shareholder vote, making this effectively a single-asset liquidation vehicle rather than a going-concern growth business.

business_model.summary: Asset Plus earns net rental income from a single Auckland office building (Munroe Lane) under an externally managed structure. Revenue is currently constrained by elevated vacancy (partial lease-up in progress); the company pays management, director, audit and other administration fees to run a very small asset base, and has no debt (0% LVR) since repaying all borrowings on the November 2024 Graham Street sale. The business is explicitly being run toward a sale-and-wind-up outcome rather than for ongoing growth.

revenue_streams.name: Munroe Lane net rental income
revenue_streams.trend: growing (from a low base as vacancy fills)

business_model.customer_type: B2B commercial office tenants (e.g., Aderant - legal/business software; Auckland Council; MILK Orthodontics; other Albany-market office/retail tenants)
business_model.geographic_mix: 100% Auckland, New Zealand (Albany, North Shore office market) - single property, single market

main_competitors: Direct landlords/sublease space in the Albany/North Shore office market
competitive_position.market_position: Sub-scale, single-asset participant in the NZ listed property sector; not a going-concern competitor for new capital or acquisitions given its wind-down posture

moat_factors.description: Munroe Lane is a 5 Star Green Star-rated, relatively modern building targeting a 5-star NABERSNZ energy rating, which helps it compete for larger corporate tenants seeking sustainable premises
0% LVR gives flexibility to fund leasing incentives from cash without refinancing risk, unlike more leveraged peers

Centuria NZ manages 80 properties and NZ$2.4bn AUM (parent Centuria Capital ~AU$21.8bn), giving market insight and leasing relationships, but this benefit accrues largely to the manager, not necessarily translating into a durable competitive advantage for a single-building shareholder vehicle

weaknesses: Single asset, single tenant-market (North Shore Auckland office) concentration risk with no diversification
Sub-scale for a listed vehicle - fixed corporate costs (directors, audit, listing/registry fees) are large relative to a $105.5m asset base and shrinking equity
External management by Centuria (19.99% shareholder via Centuria Platform Investments) creates a related-party/conflict-of-interest dynamic on fees, leasing decisions and eventual sale/wind-up timing

High and rising vacancy (only 75.6% occupied at Mar-2026, up from 65.0%, with ~3,522m2 still vacant) leaves earnings and valuation exposed to a soft Albany office leasing market (vacancy rose from 9.5% to 11.7% in the wider market over H2 2025)
No pipeline for growth - company is explicitly not seeking new acquisitions or development opportunities

growth_drivers: NOT a growth story: Asset Plus is in an explicit lease-up, sell, and wind-up trajectory - there is no acquisition or expansion strategy

Near-term 'growth' driver is completing lease-up of Munroe Lane's remaining ~3,522m2 of vacant space (Levels 1, 2 and 6), which would lift occupancy from 75.6% toward full occupancy and support a stronger sale valuation
MILK Orthodontics lease (12-year term, ground floor) expected to commence in coming months, lifting occupancy further to 75.6%+ once operational
Fully-leased passing net rent potential of $7.1-7.2m versus current passing net rent of ~$5.2m implies meaningful upside to income and valuation if vacancy is resolved

Eventual catalyst is sale of Munroe Lane followed by capital return/wind-up, which the Board has flagged is likely to require a shareholder vote within roughly the next 12-24 months (as stated in the FY2025 Chairman's letter), representing the key value-realization event rather than organic growth

business.description: 100% of the portfolio is one Auckland office building; any tenant default, structural issue, or local market deterioration disproportionately impacts the whole company

Occupancy only 75.6% at Mar-2026; Albany/North Shore office vacancy rose from 9.5% to 11.7% (Jun-Dec 2025) per CBRE, with limited large-scale tenant demand and competing sublease space undermining lease-up

Centuria (through its NZ manager and as a ~20% shareholder) earns management fees ($0.54m in FY26) irrespective of shareholder outcomes, and has board representation (director Allen Bollard no longer deemed independent from Oct-2025), creating potential misalignment on fee levels, leasing capex decisions and the timing of a sale/wind-up

Directors' fees, audit fees, listing/registry fees and insurance ($1.39m total FY26 admin costs) are a high fixed drag on a single, shrinking asset base, eroding NTA over time even before revaluation losses

financial.description: NTA has declined from 38.9 cps (Mar-2024) to 32.4 cps (Mar-2025) to 30.7 cps (Mar-2026), driven by capitalisation rate softening and capex/leasing incentives capitalised into the valuation base that are not fully recovered in rent

$3.01m of leasing incentives/costs were incurred in FY26 alone, funded from the $6.93m cash balance; further incentives will be needed to lease remaining vacant space, directly reducing the cash available for eventual distribution
Dividends are explicitly 'subject to quarterly review' - the 0.20 cps quarterly rate is not guaranteed and could be cut or suspended depending on leasing costs and cash needs

regulatory.description: Any sale of Munroe Lane or subsequent wind-up requires a shareholder vote, which introduces process risk, timing uncertainty, and the possibility that a transaction is delayed or rejected
$10.59m of tax losses remain unrecognised as a deferred tax asset; their eventual utilisation (or forfeiture on wind-up/ownership change) affects realisable shareholder value

macro.description: Elevated capitalisation/discount rates and soft office demand have driven consecutive years of unrealised valuation losses ($7.43m FY26, $7.16m FY25, $4.90m FY24); a prolonged high-rate, weak-demand environment continues to pressure both income and asset value

Property valuations are directly sensitive to capitalisation and discount rate assumptions used by independent valuers (Bayleys); a further 25bp+ softening would flow through to further NTA erosion, though the company itself is currently debt-free
Hybrid/remote work trends and oversupply of secondary office and sublease space in the North Shore market continue to constrain rental growth and lengthen lease-up periods

macro_factors.industry_outlook: NZ commercial (office) property remains in a cyclical downturn with elevated vacancy, soft rental growth, and valuers applying softer capitalisation/discount rates; a broader NZ rate-cutting cycle has provided some relief but office sector recovery has lagged industrial/retail
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - direct exposure to a single office asset in a market experiencing above-average vacancy and negative valuation momentum for four consecutive years
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High indirect sensitivity via property capitalisation/discount rates used in valuations, despite the company itself carrying zero debt (0% LVR) and no direct interest rate/refinancing risk
key_input_costs: Leasing incentives and tenant fit-out capex
Property operating expenses/outgoings on vacant space

recent_developments.event: Settled sale of 35 Graham Street; used proceeds to repay all bank debt, reducing LVR to 0%
Paid a special dividend of 5.0 cents per share following the Graham Street sale
New Aderant lease commenced 1 February 2026 across half of Level 6 (10-year term), lifting occupancy to ~74.3%

FY2026 annual results: FFO improved to $3.18m (from $0.53m), but AFFO fell to just $0.17m after $3.01m of leasing incentives/costs; total comprehensive loss narrowed to $3.16m (from $5.70m); NTA declined to 30.7 cps (from 32.4 cps) on a $7.43m unrealised revaluation loss

Munroe Lane independently revalued at $105.5m (from $107.0m), reflecting a 25bp capitalisation rate softening plus capitalised leasing capex; MILK Orthodontics secured for a 12-year ground-floor lease (not yet commenced), lifting prospective occupancy to 75.6%
Quarterly dividend of 0.20 cents per share declared for the March 2026 quarter, paid 11 June 2026; dividends remain subject to quarterly review
2026 Annual Meeting of Shareholders held at Munroe Lane, Albany, Auckland (in person and virtual)

Board has reiterated that once Munroe Lane is sufficiently leased it will look to sell the property, with any sale or subsequent wind-up requiring a shareholder vote - both decisions likely to be put to shareholders together

guidance.as_of: FY2026 Annual Results / Investor Presentation, 22 May 2026

items.target: Complete lease-up of Munroe Lane, then sell the property and put a wind-up of the Company to shareholders
items.period: Next 12-24 months (per FY2025 letter; reaffirmed FY2026)
items.notes: No formal date has been set; timing explicitly contingent on leasing progress and market conditions. This is the single most important guidance item for valuation purposes - the company should be assessed as a NTA/liquidation-value story, not a perpetual going-concern DCF.

items.target: 0.20 cents per share (March 2026 quarter, paid 11 June 2026)
items.notes: Dividend remains 'subject to quarterly review' - no fixed forward payout policy; could be reduced if further leasing incentives require cash

items.target: Future leasing costs and incentives to be funded entirely from existing cash reserves ($6.93m at Mar-2026), without drawing debt
items.notes: No new debt facility contemplated; company intends to remain unleveraged through to sale

items.target: Full occupancy of Munroe Lane (currently 75.6%, ~3,522m2 vacant across Levels 1, 2 and 6)
items.period: No fixed date - 'in the coming months' for MILK Orthodontics; balance of space ongoing
items.notes: Fully-leased net rent potential estimated at $7.1-7.2m vs current passing net rent of ~$5.2m

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Bruce Cotterill: leasing the balance of Munroe Lane remains the primary focus; market conditions remain challenging with limited large-occupier demand and elevated Albany office vacancy (11.7% as at Dec-2025, up from 9.5% in Jun-2025); the Board remains confident management is delivering the best possible outcome for shareholders and reiterates that any sale of Munroe Lane or subsequent wind-up of the Company will require shareholder approval, likely voted on together.

bull_case: Trades at a very large discount to net tangible assets (share price ~NZ$0.165-0.175 vs NTA of $0.307 per share as of Mar-2026, i.e. roughly 43-46% below stated book value), offering potential value realization if the eventual sale price is close to book
Debt-free balance sheet (0% LVR) with $6.93m of cash provides a funded runway to complete lease-up without dilutive refinancing or forced asset sales

Clear, management-articulated endgame (lease-up, sell, wind up, return capital) gives a defined catalyst path rather than open-ended going-concern uncertainty, appealing to value/special-situations investors

Recent leasing momentum (Aderant 10-year lease from Feb-2026, MILK Orthodontics 12-year lease pending) is narrowing the vacancy gap and could support a firmer sale valuation and improved FFO/AFFO run-rate
5 Star Green Star building targeting 5-star NABERSNZ rating is well-positioned versus older, less sustainable competing office stock for the tenants that remain in the market
bear_case: This is a wind-down vehicle, not a growth or income compounder - shareholders are essentially waiting on an asset sale and liquidation at an uncertain future date, with no organic growth in earnings power

AFFO (true cash profit after leasing costs) was only $0.17m in FY26 - the improved FFO headline masks the fact that leasing incentives continue to consume nearly all operating cash flow, and further incentives will be needed to complete lease-up

NTA has fallen for three consecutive years (38.9 cps to 32.4 cps to 30.7 cps) on capitalisation-rate softening and capitalised leasing costs; there is no guarantee the eventual sale price will match, let alone exceed, the current independent valuation

External management by Centuria (a ~20% shareholder) creates conflict-of-interest risk around fee levels, capex decisions and the pace/timing of the wind-up, and Centuria's board nominee is no longer classified as independent (from Oct-2025)

Sub-scale corporate overhead (directors, audit, listing/insurance costs of ~$1.39m/yr) is a persistent drag on a single, currently ~$105.5m shrinking asset base, and dividends are explicitly not guaranteed quarter to quarter

Continued high vacancy (75.6%) in a soft North Shore Auckland office market (vacancy rising to 11.7%) creates real risk that lease-up stalls, further eroding both income and the eventual realisable sale value
